**Visual Analysis of Test Image:**
- Part: Split/longitudinal section of corn stalk interior
- Color: Tan/light brown throughout
- Texture: Fibrous, shredded/degraded pith
- Notable feature: Small dark specks/dots scattered throughout the pith tissue
- No pink/red coloration (rules out Fusarium, Gibberella)
- No gray-black discoloration (rules out Charcoal stalk rot)
- No shiny black lesions (rules out Anthracnose stalk rot)

**Comparison with Diplodia stalk rot reference:**
- Reference confirms tan-brown internal discoloration of stalk pith
- Shredded fibrous tissue is characteristic
- The small dark specks in the test image are consistent with Diplodia pycnidia embedded in the pith tissue
- Color tone matches well — warm tan-brown, not black or pink

The split stalk showing tan-brown shredded pith with scattered dark pycnidia is highly characteristic of Diplodia stalk rot.
